elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New Section 15.5(b) warrants only that services "will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" for thirty (30) days; no professional-and-workmanlike / industry-standards standard of performance appears anywhere in Article 15.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 15.5(a): "each deliverable and item of software supplied by Array will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: 15.5(a) sets the conformance period at "ninety (90) days following delivery," not twelve months.
15.5(b) sets the services period at "thirty (30) days following performance," not 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 15.5: "Array shall, at Ono's election, repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable, software or services."
15.5: "...or refund the amounts paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty is added; 15.1/15.2 contain only Effective-Date corporate/authority and IP representations.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in inserted 15.5 or elsewhere in Article 15.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 15.5(a) warrants that, "for ninety (90) days following delivery, each deliverable and item of software supplied by Array will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day threshold.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 15.5(b): services "will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" for "thirty (30) days following performance."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 15.5 remedy sentence expressly provides repair or replacement of the non-conforming deliverable, software or services.
15.5 remedy sentence expressly provides "refund the amounts paid for them" as an alternative remedy.

reasons: The insertion is position-complete at the fallback level: all four fallback elements (90-day software/deliverable conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, repair/replace, refund) appear in operative language in new Section 15.5, not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no professional-and-workmanlike services standard, a 90-day rather than 12-month software period, a 30-day rather than 90-day services period, and no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add (i) "the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards", (ii) extend 15.5(a) to twelve (12) months and 15.5(b) to ninety (90) days, and (iii) add express compliance-with-applicable-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: the redline is a concise standalone insertion with no deletion or paraphrase of existing text; no carve-out edit to 15.4 was needed because that disclaimer already opens "Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement," so the new express warranty is not swallowed. Two drafting notes short of a minimality failure: "and specifications" broadens the conformance benchmark beyond the checklist's "documentation" (and Article IX defers product specifications to a future supply/quality agreement, so the reference could read as unfixed), and "at Ono's election" is more favourable than the model's vendor-option remedy — both are customer-favourable and neither adds an out-of-checklist obligation, but the drafter may wish to trim "and specifications" or tie it to specifications agreed under Article IX.

Intent is preserved: the Effective-Date representations in 15.1/15.2, the mutual implied-warranty disclaimer in 15.4, and Article IX's supply/quality-agreement mechanics all survive without contradiction; no cross-reference is broken and the warranty runs in the correct direction (Array as counterparty warranting to Ono as our client).

The "deviation" classification is correct under the detection guidance: the document contained no express performance or conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy, so an insertion was warranted rather than a rationale-only note.
